prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Added the `tasklist` extension, and `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` now works here through the new entry point; it is also in `pyproject.toml` for installs. The full suite passes (1150 tests, 112 skipped, no failures), including the new tests in `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_tasklist.py`. Not checked: flake8 isn't installed, so I only checked line lengths by hand, and I didn't build the docs, so the new page's rendered examples haven't been run. Nothing is committed. The changelog entry has no issue number because there isn't an issue, and I left the version at 3.11.2. Behavior choices: only the marker is replaced, so the following space stays (`<input ... /> foo`). With the default `xhtml` output the attributes appear as `disabled="disabled"`, and as bare `disabled` with `output_format='html'`. Footnote items themselves never become tasks, though lists nested inside a footnote can. An empty `item_class` adds no class.

check.why: task lists everywhere, options, entry point, docs, tests and changelog
